_comment: nexus-gateway provider registry. Callers address a model as {provider}:{model} (or {provider}/{model}); the prefix is looked up here and everything after the FIRST separator is the model id sent upstream. EVERY provider egresses through Cloudflare AI Gateway — dispatch() refuses an entry without a slug and no direct-fetch code path exists. This map IS the allowlist: a prefix that is not here cannot be reached, which is what stops a virtual key spending against a provider you never enabled. To add a provider: register it in AI Gateway (or use a native slug), then add one entry — usually just {slug, secret}. Everything else has a default.

defaults._comment: Applied to every provider unless overridden. Kept separate so the common case is genuinely empty config.

aliases._comment: Alias → canonical. Callers migrate naming at their own pace without duplicating an entry.

nvidia_nim.note: 6-key rotation is Worker-side — AI Gateway cannot rotate keys. Worth ~6x the per-key rate limit.

zai.note: Coding-plan endpoint sits at a non-standard path; AIG appends it to the base_url verbatim.

zai_anthropic.note: The ONLY route where a signed Anthropic thinking chain survives — body is forwarded untouched.

anthropic.note: Direct api.anthropic.com via AIG's native slug. Body forwarded untouched, so signed thinking chains survive. anthropic-version/-beta are forwarded; anthropic-workspace-id comes from ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID when the key is not workspace-scoped.

cloudflare.note: Workers AI rejects the tools field.

dynamic.note: AI Gateway DYNAMIC ROUTES. Addressed as the literal model `dynamic/{route-name}` on the gateway's `compat` endpoint, so the prefix must survive (keepPrefix) — a bare route name gets `Chat completion bad format`. `compat` is a real AIG path segment, not a registered provider, hence no `custom-` prefix. The route picks the provider itself; every node of the routes we ship is `custom-nvidia`, so the NVIDIA pool key is the right outbound credential. ⚠️ A route that mixes PROVIDERS cannot work this way — one Authorization header would be sent to every hop; that case needs AI Gateway stored keys (BYOK).
